AG - News, Notes & Nugs
10/14/2026
Corn and wheat a pinkish shade of red and Beans up 3-4 at the morning pause.
Chinese state buyers purchased 8-10 Panamax cargoes of US soybeans this week, the first such deals since the September summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Washington, three trade sources told Reuters on Wednesday. The cargoes are for shipment from December onwards, they added. The market had been awaiting signs of renewed Chinese buying after a weeks-long hiatus, partly because of weak demand during the country's week-long National Day holiday earlier this month. The latest purchases were made by state-owned trading firms, the traders said. The companies paid premiums of $3.10 to $3.20 per bushel over the January Chicago Board of Trade soybean contract SF27, one of the traders said. Each Panamax cargo carries around 65,000 metric tons of soybeans.
China, the world's largest soy buyer, imported 11.88 million metric tons of soybeans in September, down 7.7% from the same month last year, data from the General Administration of Customs of China showed. Soybean imports in September fell from 12.87 million tons a year earlier and were down 2.1% from 12.14 million tons in August. From January to September, soybean arrivals in the world's biggest buyer totalled 86.08 million tons, the data showed.
China's soybean crushing sector faces significant overcapacity with daily crushing capacity of imports set to exceed 520,000 metric tons by the end of the year, an industry official said on Wednesday. Lv Xiuping, a member of a committee of the ruling Communist Party Committee at state-run COFCO Oils and Oilseeds, who also holds the post of chief accountant, made the remarks at an agricultural conference in the northeastern city of Dalian.
Taiwan's MFIG purchasing group made no purchase in an international tender seeking about 65,000 metric tons of animal feed corn that closed on Wednesday, European traders said. Prices offered were regarded as too high, traders said. Traders believed importers were hoping for further falls in corn prices as the unexpectedly largeUS harvest progresses. The lowest price offer was said to be a premium of 224.0 US cents a bushel cost and freight (c&f) included over the Chicago March 2027 corn contract CH27, they said. The offer was submitted for 65,000 tons of US-origin yellow corn by trading house CHS, traders said. This was followed by an offer for 58,500 tons of Brazilian yellow corn at a premium of 225.5 cents c&f over Chicago said to have been submitted by trading house ETG. The tender was dominated by US and Brazilian corn, with five trading companies each offering 65,000 tons of US corn and eight companies offering consignments of between 58,000 and 65,000 tons from Brazil. No offers were reported for Argentine or South African corn.
Intercontinental Exchange ICE plans to launch its first cattle and hog futures contracts on December 7, the market operator said on Tuesday, in a challenge to rival CME Group. The New York Stock Exchange parent intends to offer physically delivered US live cattle futures, along with financially settled futures for live cattle, feeder cattle and lean hogs, pending regulatory review, according to a notice. The first listed month for physically delivered live cattle will be June 2027, the notice said.
